arxiv-1911-06567.title: Reconciling Event Structures with Modern Multiprocessors
arxiv-1911-06567.creator: Evgenii Moiseenko, Anton Podkopaev, Ori Lahav, Orestis Melkonian, Viktor Vafeiadis
arxiv-1911-06567.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Evgenii Moiseenko, Anton Podkopaev, Ori Lahav, Orestis Melkonian, Viktor Vafeiadis. 𝖶𝖾𝖺𝗄𝖾𝗌𝗍𝗆𝗈 \mathsf{Weakestmo} is a recently proposed memory consistency model that uses event structures to resolve the infamous “out-of-thin-air” problem and to enable efficient compilation to hardware. Nevertheless, this latter property—compilation correctness—has not yet been formally established.

arxiv-2001-06296.title: Overly Optimistic Prediction Results on Imbalanced Data: a Case Study of Flaws and Benefits when Applying Over-sampling
arxiv-2001-06296.creator: Gilles Vandewiele, Isabelle Dehaene, György Kovács, Lucas Sterckx, Olivier Janssens, Femke Ongenae, Femke De Backere, Filip De Turck, Kristien Roelens, Johan Decruyenaere, Sofie Van Hoecke, Thomas Demeester
arxiv-2001-06296.description: Abstract Information extracted from electrohysterography recordings could potentially prove to be an interesting additional source of information to estimate the risk on preterm birth. Recently, a large number of studies have reported near-perfect results to distinguish between recordings of patients that will deliver term or preterm using a public resource, called the Term/Preterm Electrohysterogram database.

arxiv-2010-09471.title: Finding Cut-Offs in Leaderless Rendez-Vous Protocols is Easy Thanks: The last author was affiliated with Technische Universität München when this work was done.
arxiv-2010-09471.creator: A. R. Balasubramanian ORCID:0000-0002-7258-5445, Javier Esparza ORCID:0000-0001-9862-4919, Mikhail Raskin ORCID:0000-0002-6660-5673
arxiv-2010-09471.description: Abstract . In rendez-vous protocols an arbitrarily large number of indistinguishable finite-state agents interact in pairs. The cut-off problem asks if there exists a number B B such that all initial configurations of the protocol with at least B B agents in a given initial state can reach a final configuration with all agents in a given final state.

arxiv-2210-04629.title: Investigation of inverse design of multilayer thin-films with conditional invertible Neural Networks
arxiv-2210-04629.creator: Alexander Luce, Ali Mahdavi, Heribert Wankerl, Florian Marquardt
arxiv-2210-04629.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexander Luce, Ali Mahdavi, Heribert Wankerl, Florian Marquardt. The task of designing optical multilayer thin-films regarding a given target is currently solved using gradient-based optimization in conjunction with methods that can introduce additional thin-film layers. Recently, Deep Learning and Reinforcement Learning have been been introduced to the task of designing thin-films with great success, however a trained network is usually only able to become proficient for a single target and must be retrained if the optical targets are varied.

arxiv-2211-15774.title: Decentralized Learning with Multi-Headed Distillation
arxiv-2211-15774.creator: Andrey Zhmoginov, Mark Sandler, Nolan Miller, Gus Kristiansen, Max Vladymyrov
arxiv-2211-15774.description: Abstract Decentralized learning with private data is a central problem in machine learning. We propose a novel distillation-based decentralized learning technique that allows multiple agents with private non-iid data to learn from each other, without having to share their data, weights or weight updates.

arxiv-2212-09628.title: The implications of Ultra-Faint Dwarf Galaxy Reticulum II on the common envelope jets supernova r-process scenario
arxiv-2212-09628.creator: Aldana Grichener, Noam Soker
arxiv-2212-09628.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Aldana Grichener, Noam Soker. We show that the common envelope jets supernova (CEJSN) r-process scenario is compatible with very recent observationally determined properties of the stars in the ultra faint dwarf (UFD) galaxy Reticulum II that are strongly enhanced in r-process elements. These new results, like efficient mixing of the r-process elements in the Reticulum II galaxy, have some implications on the CEJSN r-process scenario for UFD galaxies.

arxiv-2301-08279.title: UV and H ​ α \mathrm{H}\alpha HST observations of 6 GASP jellyfish galaxies Journal: ApJ Python, astropy ( The Astropy Collaboration 2018 ) , synphot ( STScI Development Team 2020 )
arxiv-2301-08279.creator: Marco Gullieuszik, Eric Giunchi, Bianca M. Poggianti, Alessia Moretti, Claudia Scarlata, Daniela Calzetti, Ariel Werle, Anita Zanella, Mario Radovich, Callum Bellhouse, Daniela Bettoni, Andrea Franchetto, Jacopo Fritz, Yara L. Jaffé, Sean L. McGee, Matilde Mingozzi, Alessandro Omizzolo, Stephanie To
arxiv-2301-08279.description: Abstract Star-forming, H ​ α \mathrm{H}\alpha -emitting clumps are found embedded in the gaseous tails of galaxies undergoing intense ram pressure stripping in galaxy clusters, so-called jellyfish galaxies. These clumps offer a unique opportunity to study star formation under extreme conditions, in the absence of an underlying disk and embedded within the hot intracluster medium.

arxiv-2301-11927.title: PACE Solver Description: A Heuristic Directed Feedback Vertex Set Problem Algorithm
arxiv-2301-11927.creator: Andrei Arhire, Paul Diac
arxiv-2301-11927.description: Abstract A feedback vertex set of a graph is a set of nodes with the property that every cycle contains at least one vertex from the set i.e. the removal of all vertices from a feedback vertex set leads to an acyclic graph.

arxiv-2307-15208.title: Generative AI for Medical Imaging: extending the MONAI Framework
arxiv-2307-15208.creator: Walter H. L. Pinaya, Mark S. Graham, Eric Kerfoot, Petru-Daniel Tudosiu, Jessica Dafflon, Virginia Fernandez, Pedro Sanchez, Julia Wolleb, Pedro F. da Costa, Ashay Patel, Hyungjin Chung, Can Zhao, Wei Peng, Zelong Liu, Xueyan Mei, Oeslle Lucena, Jong Chul Ye, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris, Prerna Dogra, And
arxiv-2307-15208.description: Abstract Recent advances in generative AI have brought incredible breakthroughs in several areas, including medical imaging. These generative models have tremendous potential not only to help safely share medical data via synthetic datasets but also to perform an array of diverse applications, such as anomaly detection, image-to-image translation, denoising, and MRI reconstruction.

arxiv-2408-03979.title: Speaker Adaptation for Quantised End-to-End ASR Models
arxiv-2408-03979.creator: Qiuming Zhao, Guangzhi Sun, Chao Zhang, Mingxing Xu, Thomas Fang Zheng
arxiv-2408-03979.description: Abstract End-to-end models have shown superior performance for automatic speech recognition (ASR) [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] . However, such models are often very large in size and thus challenging to deploy on resource-constrained edge devices.

arxiv-2409-19960.title: TROPE: TRaining-Free Object-Part Enhancement for Seamlessly Improving Fine-Grained Zero-Shot Image Captioning
arxiv-2409-19960.creator: Joshua Feinglass and Yezhou Yang
arxiv-2409-19960.description: Abstract Zero-shot inference, where pre-trained models perform tasks without specific training data, is an exciting emergent ability of large models like CLIP. Although there has been considerable exploration into enhancing zero-shot abilities in image captioning (IC) for popular datasets such as MSCOCO and Flickr8k, these approaches fall short with fine-grained datasets like CUB, FLO, UCM-Captions, and Sydney-Captions.

arxiv-2411-06075.title: Barrow Cosmology and Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis
arxiv-2411-06075.creator: Ahmad Sheykhi and Ava Shahbazi
arxiv-2411-06075.description: Abstract Using thermodynamics-gravity conjecture, we present the formal derivation of the modified Friedmann equations inspired by the Barrow entropy, S ∼ A 1 + δ / 2 S\sim A^{1+\delta/2} , where 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1 0\leq\delta\leq 1 is the Barrow exponent and A A is the horizon area.

arxiv-2506-18275.title: Phase transition of descending phase retrieval algorithms
arxiv-2506-18275.creator: Mihailo Stojnic
arxiv-2506-18275.description: Abstract Abstract We study theoretical limits of descending phase retrieval algorithms. Utilizing Random duality theory (RDT) we develop a generic program that allows statistical characterization of various algorithmic performance metrics. Through these we identify the concepts of parametric manifold and its funneling points as key mathematical objects that govern the underlying algorithms’ behavior.

arxiv-2506-21200.title: A Lebesgue variant of the additive square problem
arxiv-2506-21200.creator: Ingrid Vukusic
arxiv-2506-21200.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ingrid Vukusic. We prove that for every Lebesgue measurable function f : ℝ → { v 1 , … , v t } ⊆ ℝ f\colon\mathbb{R}\to\{v_{1},\ldots,v_{t}\}\subseteq\mathbb{R} there exist x ∈ ℝ x\in\mathbb{R} , y > 0 y>0 such that ∫ x x + y f ​ 𝑑 λ = ∫ x + y x + 2 ​ y f ​ 𝑑 λ . \int_{x}^{x+y}f\,d\lambda=\int_{x+y}^{x+2y}f\,d\lambda. This can be seen as a variant of the classical additive square problem for infinite words over finite alphabets.

arxiv-2510-04631.title: Contrastive Learning Using Graph Embeddings for Domain Adaptation of Language Models in the Process Industry
arxiv-2510-04631.creator: Anastasia Zhukova, Jonas Lührs, Christian E. Lobmüller, Bela Gipp
arxiv-2510-04631.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anastasia Zhukova, Jonas Lührs, Christian E. Lobmüller, Bela Gipp. Recent trends in NLP utilize knowledge graphs (KGs) to enhance pretrained language models by incorporating additional knowledge from the graph structures to learn domain-specific terminology or relationships between documents that might otherwise be overlooked. This paper explores how SciNCL, a graph-aware neighborhood contrastive learning methodology originally designed for scientific publications, can be applied to the process industry domain, where text logs contain crucial information about daily operations and are often structured as sparse KGs.

arxiv-2605-20988.title: A Sharper Picture of Generalization in Transformers
arxiv-2605-20988.creator: Paul Lintilhac, Sair Shaikh

arxiv-2606-00314.title: Electronic screening of the friction acting on ions and water molecules in narrow carbon nanotubes
arxiv-2606-00314.creator: A.W.C. Lau 1, J.B. Sokoloff 1,2

pmc-10623535.title: Interactive effects of CDKN2B‐AS1 gene polymorphism and habitual risk factors on oral cancer
pmc-10623535.creator: Jung‐Chun Yeh, Yi‐Tzu Chen, Ying‐Erh Chou, Shih‐Chi Su, Lun‐Ching Chang, Yen‐Lin Chen, Chiao‐Wen Lin, Shun‐Fa Yang
pmc-10623535.description: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a common malignant disease associated with a high mortality rate and heterogeneous disease aetiology. Cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2B antisense RNA 1 (CDKN2B‐AS1), is a long noncoding RNA that has been shown to act as a scaffold, sponge, or signal hub to promote carcinogenesis.

pmc-11297649.title: Efficacy of tranexamic acid versus placebo in reducing blood loss during burn excisional surgery: a multi-center, double-blind, parallel, randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial (TRANEX)
pmc-11297649.creator: R K Gigengack, J Slob, A Meij-de Vries, E Bosma, S A Loer, J S H A Koopman, C H van der Vlies
pmc-11297649.description: BackgroundDespite an increase in knowledge, blood loss during burn excisional surgery remains a major challenge and is an independent predictor of mortality. During burn surgery, limited measures are available to control the bleeding. Increased fibrinolysis could be one of the contributing factors of blood loss during burn excisional surgery.

pmc-11480328.title: Image segmentation for pest detection of crop leaves by improvement of regional convolutional neural network
pmc-11480328.creator: Xianchuan Wu, Yuling Liu, Mingjing Xing, Chun Yang, Shaoyong Hong
pmc-11480328.description: Pest detection is important for crop cultivation. Crop leaf is the main place of pest invasion. Current technologies to detect crop pests have constraints, such as low efficiency, storage demands and limited precision. Image segmentation is a fast and efficient computer-aided detection technology. High resolution image capture solidly supports the crucial processes in discerning pests from images.

pmc-11625903.title: Structural relationships between psychological factors and college adjustment among medical students in South Korea: focusing on helicopter parenting and respectful parenting
pmc-11625903.creator: Jin Young Lee, Ie Byung Park, So Jung Yune, Kwi Hwa Park
pmc-11625903.description: PurposeThis study aims to determine the impact of helicopter parenting and respectful parenting on medical students’ mindset, grit, self-directedness, and college adjustment.MethodsThis study constructed a hypothetical model based on the relationship between helicopter parenting, respectful parenting, mindset, grit, self-directedness, and college adjustment. It set up a structural model to test the fit of the model based on empirical data.

pmc-11715860.title: Association between everyday perceived discrimination and cognitive function as mediated by depression in diverse populations: A HABS‐HD Study
pmc-11715860.creator: Edna Patricia Mendoza, Emma Nolan, Nicole Phillips, Robert Barber, Sid E O'Bryant, Zhengyang Zhou
pmc-11715860.description: BackgroundPrevious research suggests that perceived discrimination is associated with cognitive function impairment, and such association is mediated by depression. With minority populations continuously growing, it is crucial to investigate such relationships in diverse populations. This study aims to examine and compare the above relationships among non‐Hispanic white (NHW), Mexican American (MA), and African American (AA) participants.

pmc-11969357.title: Weave Technique for Reconstruction of Medial Collateral Ligament and Posterior Oblique Ligament: A Functional Percutaneous Approach Using Gracilis Tendon
pmc-11969357.creator: Luis Fernando Zukanovich Funchal, Rafael Ortiz, Lucio S R Ernlund, Diego Costa Astur, Moisés Cohen, Riccardo Gomes Gobbi, Guilherme Moreira de Abreu e Silva
pmc-11969357.description: Background:Injury to the medial collateral ligament (MCL) is common. MCL injuries, with impairment of its superficial portion, associated with the deep portion, lead to valgus instability and extrusion of the medial meniscus, resulting in instability and increased pressure in the medial compartment, with consequent damage to the cartilage. We can synthesize this set of structures as the medial meniscocapsular complex.

pmc-12512330.title: Recrudescent severe malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum following treatment in a Taiwanese patient: a case report
pmc-12512330.creator: Yu-Chuan Tseng, Meng-Yu Cheng, Peter Bor-Chian Lin, Shih-Fen Hsu, Jen-Jen Hsu, Yi-Cheng Shen, Mao-Wang Ho, Chiung-Tzu Hsiao, Po-Ren Hsueh
pmc-12512330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundSevere malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum remains a life-threatening disease, particularly in non-immune individuals returning from endemic regions. While prompt treatment can usually achieve parasite clearance, recrudescence after initial recovery is rare and presents unique diagnostic and management difficulties.

pmc-12523305.title: Beyond Nerve Entrapment: A Narrative Review of Muscle–Tendon Pathologies in Deep Gluteal Syndrome
pmc-12523305.creator: Yong Hyun Yoon, Ji Hyo Hwang, Ho won Lee, MinJae Lee, Chanwool Park, Jonghyeok Lee, Seungbeom Kim, JaeYoung Lee, Jeimylo C. de Castro, King Hei Stanley Lam, Teinny Suryadi, Kwan Hyun Youn
pmc-12523305.description: Deep Gluteal Syndrome (DGS) has traditionally been defined as a clinical entity caused by sciatic nerve (SN) entrapment. However, recent anatomical and imaging studies suggest that muscle- and tendon-origin pathologies—including enthesopathy—may also serve as primary pain generators. This narrative review aims to broaden the current understanding of DGS by integrating muscle and tendon pathologies into its diagnostic and therapeutic framework.

pmc-12540773.title: Review for optical metalens based on metasurfaces: fabrication and applications
pmc-12540773.creator: Zhikai Hu, Manna Gu, Ying Tian, Chenxia Li, Mingmin Zhu, Haomiao Zhou, Bo Fang, Zhi Hong, Xufeng Jing
pmc-12540773.description: Metalens is the next generation of optical metasurfaces for compact imaging, sensing, and display applications that allow the phase, polarization, frequency, amplitude, angular momentum, etc. of the incident light to be designed with high degrees of freedom to meet the application requirements, which has attracted broad interest in the field of planar optics.

pmc-12552833.title: Palliative Care for Children and Adults With Inherited Metabolic Disease in Europe: An Underutilised Service for Supportive Treatment and Care
pmc-12552833.creator: Anja Lee, Yngve Thomas Bliksrud, Michela Onali, Julia Neugebauer, Francois Eyskens, Dorothea Haas, Karin Mossler, Antije Enekwe, Beata Kiec‐Wilk, Lien My Diep, Cinzia Maria Bellettato, Boris Zernikow, Maurizio Scarpa, Shamima Rahman, Trine Tangeraas, MetabERN collaboration group on palliative care
pmc-12552833.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Palliative care should be an integral part of follow‐up for patients with life‐limiting/life‐threatening conditions, irrespective of age and diagnosis. Many patients with inherited metabolic disorders (IMD) have palliative care needs due to multi‐systemic conditions without curative treatment options.

pmc-13070127.title: A Tale as Old as Time: Contraception Concerns in the 21st Century
pmc-13070127.creator: Rachel Margaret Bottomley-Wise, Amie Woodward, Adenike Okanlawon, Amanda J Mason-Jones
pmc-13070127.description: Historical inconsistencies in contraception research have led to concerns about side effects regarding hormonal contraception. Today, concerns about the hormonal contraceptive pill are still ongoing. The side effects from hormonal contraception and prevailing socioeconomic barriers to effective contraception have heralded in the use of Mobile Health (mHealth) applications as birth control methods.

pmc-13083925.title: TDP-43 pathology triggers neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment by inducing microglial necroptosis
pmc-13083925.creator: Shenrui Guo, Hongfu Jin, Hui Sun, Shuo Huang, Yuanyuan Chen, Yuge Chang, Yu Zhang, Lin Ding, Suyun Chen, Chenglai Fu, Yafu Yin, Weiwei Cheng
pmc-13083925.description: Pathological TAR DNA-binding protein-43 (TDP-43) is a defining feature of several neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the mechanism by which TDP-43 pathology disrupts microglial function and drives neuroinflammation remains unclear.

pmc-13146330.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1379 CLINICAL SEVERITY AND OUTCOMES IN TANDEM OCCLUSION STROKE: THE ROLE OF COMBINED REPERFUSION STRATEGIES: A SINGLE-CENTER EXPERIENCE
pmc-13146330.creator: Tatiana Stupac, Veronica Spinei, Levca Anastasia, Alexandru Grumeza, Ion Preguza
pmc-13146330.description: Background and aimsTandem occlusions, involving simultaneous extracranial internal carotid artery (ICA) and intracranial large-vessel occlusions, are associated with high stroke severity and poor natural prognosis. Rapid and effective reperfusion is therefore critical to limit neurological damage. We aimed to assess the clinical impact of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) prior to mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with tandem occlusions.

pmc-13346549.title: P-60 - THE ‘SUPER FLU’ THAT WASN’T: THE IMPACT OF THE H3N2 SUBCLADE K ON THE SCOTTISH POPULATION, 2025/26
pmc-13346549.creator: Mr Ebrahim Makhoul, Dr Stefanie Wilson, Dr Masoumeh Rezaie, Mr Allan Mcleod, Dr Kirsty Morrison, Mr Safraj Shahul Hameed, Mr John Wood, Prof Rory Gunson, Dr Kimberly Marsh
pmc-13346549.description: BackgroundSeasonal influenza remains unpredictable due to continual viral evolution, particularly within A(H3N2) lineages. Novel subclades can alter transmission, severity, and vaccine effectiveness (VE), underscoring the importance of pathogen-specific surveillance. In 2025/26, Scotland and other European countries identified a new H3N2 subclade, speculatively labelled ’Super Flu’, prompting intensified monitoring.

pmc-13476626.title: Ninety-day venous thromboembolism incidence and associated risk factors after total and reverse shoulder arthroplasty: a national database analysis
pmc-13476626.creator: Lina H Elias, Marisol Allen, Olufunmilola Adeleye, Anup A Shah, Midhat Patel, Evan S Lederman
pmc-13476626.description: BackgroundVenous thromboembolism (VTE), including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, is an uncommon but potentially serious complication following total shoulder arthroplasty. This study evaluated patient factors associated with post-operative (PO) VTE after anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (aTSA) and reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA).MethodsA retrospective cohort study was performed using the PearlDiver database.
